title: Sports radio to try in Malta
intro: Over-the-air radio only: FM and DAB+ receiver leads, dated and recurring sports programmes, and a separate fixture/market reference. No named trip-week match has yet met all checks for Malta terrestrial carriage. Web streams, UK schedules and overlapping kickoffs are not substitutes for that evidence.

records.description: Malta's terrestrial picture is now much clearer than a directory list. A dated observation of the Maltese multiplexes on 13 January 2026 shows the sports services on block 6C: a service labelled “Sports Channel” (SId C02F) and Radio Sportiva (SId C02A). Block 6A carries BBC World Service and Rai RadioUno, and block 12A carried no sports service at all. That means real live-sport radio does exist over the air here — Rai Radio 1's weekend football programme, which uses live match commentators for Serie A and Serie B, is carried on 6A and both its air days fall inside the trip. What is still missing is the last link: no station has published which specific match it will commentate on 17 or 18 October, and no receiver scan has been made in the hotel room or at the venue. Plan to scan, but do not promise yourself a named match.
records.notes: Evidence read 11 October 2026: observed Maltese multiplex service tables and technical data at https://www.wohnort.org/dab/malta.html (tables captioned 'Source: Observations, 13.01.2026'; page updated 30 January 2026); official Rai programme page at https://www.raiplaysound.it/programmi/tuttoilcalciominutoperminuto ; operator channel directory https://dab.com.mt/channels/ ; station schedule pages https://www.radiosportiva.com/palinsesto/ and https://netfm.com.mt/ ; BBC dated episode records https://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/w1730c92ck0m2cw.json and https://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/w1730c92ck0q313.json . records.name: Receiver checklist · what a Maltese DAB+ service actually requires
records.area: Malta — national FM and DAB+ coverage
records.address: Not applicable — receiver guidance
records.hours: Check your own receiver's specifications before departure. Malta's national services are HE-AAC v2 DAB+; a Band III DAB+ tuner is required. Scan locally before relying on any programme.
records.price range: Not published here; local receiver prices were not checked
records.description: For FM, check that the receiver tunes the exact Maltese frequency with an appropriate tuning step. For the digital services use a real DAB+ Band III receiver: an HD Radio badge, or an older DAB-only label, does not establish DAB+ support, and a US-market HD Radio will not receive DAB+. The observed Maltese multiplexes use DAB+ stereo HE-AAC v2 at low bitrates — 32 kbit/s for BBC World Service, Rai RadioUno, Radio Sportiva and “Sports Channel” — so speech-grade audio on news and sport services is normal rather than a fault. A phone app or web stream uses internet access and does not satisfy this guide's over-the-air requirement.
records.notes: Digi B's own site describes DAB+ reception with a suitable tuner: https://dab.com.mt/ . Observed Maltese multiplex service tables with codecs and bitrates: https://www.wohnort.org/dab/malta.html ('Source: Observations, 13.01.2026'). Industry directory: https://www.worlddab.org/why-dab-plus/countries/malta/multiplexes . FM frequencies: https://ba.org.mt/stations-licenced . Earlier BBC guidance https://www.bbc.co.uk/worldservice/mobile/institutional/2009/03/000000_digitallisting.shtml is not a reason to reject every modern UK-purchased DAB+ set. Check the manufacturer's actual codec, band and tuning specifications. No model, purchase stock or room reception was tested.

records.address: Not applicable — broadcast service. Block resolved to 6C (185.360 MHz); 12A was part of the same dated observation and carried no sports service, so 6C is the tuning target.

records.price range: Free-to-air if broadcast; DAB+ receiver required (hardware price not checked)
records.description: Two independent lines of evidence now converge on block 6C for a service labelled “Sports Channel”: an independent Malta directory entry and a dated observation of the 6C multiplex on 13 January 2026 that lists the service by service ID and bitrate. A 2023 enthusiast field report of the same DIGI B 3 / 6C ensemble labelled it as carrying talkSPORT programming. What is established: the service label, the service ID (C02F), the bitrate (32 kbit/s), the block and the fact that the service persisted into the January 2026 observation. What is not established: what it broadcasts on 13–19 October 2026, whether it is still a talkSPORT relay, and whether it can be received indoors at the hotel or at the venue.
records.notes: Converging evidence: dated 6C service table at https://www.wohnort.org/dab/malta.html ('Sports Channel', SId C02F, 32 kbit/s DAB+ stereo HE-AAC v2, 'Source: Observations, 13.01.2026'); independent directory entry at https://radioinmalta.com/en/dab/6c.php (C02F, DAB+ HE-AAC v2; page marked under construction); historic field report of the same ensemble at https://www.radioblog.eu/2023/10/16/dab-programme-auf-malta-teil-2-kanal-6c-digi-b-3/ which labels the service '(Talk Sport)' and gives talksport.com. The contradictory 12A entry is recorded separately: https://www.worlddab.org/why-dab-plus/countries/malta/multiplexes . Operator consumer directory: https://dab.com.mt/channels/ . talkSPORT carriage and rights in its own markets: https://www.premierleague.com/en/about/partners/talksport . The 2023 report is historical and third-party: it is not evidence of content on 17–18 October 2026. No receiver scan; at 32 kbit/s HE-AAC v2 the audio is speech-grade. The crowd-edited talkSPORT article's own frequency infobox now lists 'DAB+: 6C (Malta)' beside 'DAB+: 11D/12A (Digital One)', and states that outside the UK and Ireland talkSPORT carries live commentary of every Premier League match in several languages including English — that is third-party corroboration of the 6C lead and of the wider English-language distribution, not proof of what the Maltese service relays on a given matchday (<https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Talksport>). The WorldDAB 12A table that started the conflict repeats several services also listed on 6C and carries '6c_Test7' / '6c Test12' labels, which hints at a metadata/assignment problem on that side; it remains unexplained. The operator's consumer channel directory renders no sports tile, but a 'Load more' control means that page was never read in full.

The parallel branch could NOT fetch the 5 Live Sport studio-shows page (https://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/b0070hx6/broadcasts/upcoming) and therefore logged those entries only as an unverified lead; this record's successful direct read of that page supersedes the lead and closes it. Practical split for this trip, from a dated 13 January 2026 observation of the multiplexes: block 6A carries BBC World Service, Rai RadioUno/Due/Tre, Net FM, Vibe and most Maltese services; block 6C carries the sports pair — a service labelled “Sports Channel” (SId C02F) and Radio Sportiva (SId C02A) — plus the UK relays LBC 97.3, Capital, Gold, Smooth, Jazz FM and others; block 12A carried the Smooth Platform services with no sports service on that date.
